_about: Field terms for F344, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

uhecr.definition: a charged particle from space, a proton or heavier nucleus, arriving with an energy above about 1e18 electronvolts; it is recorded through the shower of secondary particles it makes in the atmosphere
uhecr.excludes: photons and neutrinos, and the far more common cosmic rays of lower energy

eev.definition: an exaelectronvolt, 1e18 electronvolts, or 1e9 GeV, carried by a single particle
eev.excludes: the total energy of the shower in a detector, which is spread over many secondary particles

lattice-spacing.definition: the distance between neighbouring points of a grid on which space is modelled; on a grid, waves shorter than about twice the spacing cannot exist and the speed of a wave depends on its direction
lattice-spacing.excludes: the Planck length, which is a scale built from constants and not a measured grid

cubic-harmonic.definition: the simplest pattern on a sphere with the symmetry of a cube: here x^4 + y^4 + z^4 minus its average, largest along the six cube axes and smallest along the eight diagonals
cubic-harmonic.excludes: a dipole, a single hot spot, or any pattern that a rotation of the cube by a right angle would change

exposure.definition: how much of each part of the sky a detector watched over time; a ground array sees some declinations far more than others, so an isotropic sky still looks uneven in its data
exposure.excludes: the number of events, which is exposure times the true flux

ra-scramble.definition: a control sky made by keeping each event's declination and giving it a random right ascension; the Earth's rotation makes a ground array's exposure nearly even in right ascension, so the scramble keeps the exposure and removes any pattern
ra-scramble.excludes: a fully random sky, which would ignore the detector's exposure

benjamini-hochberg.definition: a rule that raises a set of p values to control the expected share of false discoveries among the tests called significant; the smallest raw p is multiplied by the number of tests and larger ones by less
benjamini-hochberg.excludes: an uncorrected p value read on its own when several tests were run

power.definition: the share of planted skies, each with a pattern of known strength, in which the search finds the pattern at its preregistered threshold
power.excludes: the chance that a pattern exists in the real sky
